title: nem Splits Them: Negation Sends the Prefix Behind the Verb

sections.title: nem still wants the spot right before the verb
sections.content: You already know that nem parks itself directly in front of the verb it negates — Nem dolgozom, Károly nem tanul. That rule doesn't change with a prefixed verb. But the prefix can't stay glued to the front any more, because nem needs exactly that spot. So the prefix jumps to the other side of the verb instead, landing right after it: Nem megyek be, not Nem bemegyek.

items.spanish: Ma nem megyek be a boltba.
items.english: Today I'm not going into the shop.

items.spanish: Még nem eszem meg a levest.
items.english: I'm still not eating up the soup / I haven't finished the soup yet.

sections.content: Watch for the reverse mistake too: Nem bemegyek is not natural Hungarian word order — nem and the bare verb stay glued together, and the prefix parks itself at the very end instead. már works the opposite way, sitting happily in front of the whole glued verb in a statement: Már bemegyek a boltba ('I'm already on my way into the shop').
